newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia launches supply craft for Mir.
newsitem.headline: Russia launches supply craft for Mir.

text.p: Russia launched a Progress-34 cargo craft on Sunday to take crucial supplies to the two Russian cosmonauts and U.S. astronaut aboard its troubled Mir space station, Russian news agencies said.
The unmanned craft blasted off on on schedule at 1604 GMT, a spokesman for the Military Space Forces said. It is due to dock with Mir with its supplies of food, water, fuel and equipment on April 8.

NASA officials said on Friday the supply ship would also carry a repair kit for Mir's oxygen generator, fresh oxygen generating chemicals and gear to further patch up leaks which had developed in its cooling system.
They said the leaks had knocked out a device used to maintain breathable air on board, but that backup systems were running and that the leaks would be repaired at the weekend.
The U.S. space agency will nevertheless review safety on Mir before sending any more astronauts to live and work there, a senior NASA official said.
An official from the Russian Space Agency, which coordinates manned space flights, said there were also big problems getting fuel for the Soyuz booster carrying the Progress into space.
